answer: A practical Sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can influence a shared task queue. When an agent’s signed work is independently checked and found fraudulent, the protocol slashes that stake; honest agents recover theirs after review. This does not prove one person controls only one identity, but makes flooding costly: an attacker must lock capital in every fake account and risks losing it. In a willow, nectar, and crystal marketplace, repeated fabricated bids therefore burn real funds rather than earning free influence.
